Photoreal live-action, Ferrier's farm, Utah, 1860, oil lamp, black shadow, 35 mm film grain.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:08. The camera is at the window level with his eyes, an arm's length from him, a 90mm lens. The lamp is the light, from the LEFT. At the first frame John Ferrier's face fills the CENTRE of the frame, half the frame height. The camera pans left across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth as the blue-black glass keeps the right third and the sill keeps the bottom edge, from 00:00 to 00:06. <Subject 1> (S1), on screen, a tall spare man in his middle fifties, with a clipped English voice at an even pace, says: <d>[English] Then we ride tonight. Every acre of it can stay.</d> His mouth shapes every syllable as the line is heard and closes on the last word. At 00:06, as the line ends, his eyes come round from the glass to the lens. At 00:07 his jaw sets on the words, then his hand lifts off the sill and closes, and the lift continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:08 the camera is panning left through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
